name: z80dasm
desc: Disassembler for the Zilog Z80 microprocessor and compatibles
why: A disassembler for Z80 binaries, a doorway into retro hardware and the machine code of classic computers and game consoles.

brief.what_it_is: z80dasm is a command-line disassembler for the Zilog Z80 microprocessor and compatible chips. It takes a binary file, such as a ROM dump or program image, and writes out Z80 assembly source. It can read label names from a symbol file and use code and data section information to produce a cleaner listing. The output can be reassembled to the same binary with z80asm, zasm, or the original Zilog assembler.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says it can be used to reverse engineer programs and operating systems for 1980s microcomputers that used the Z80, such as the Sinclair ZX81 and Spectrum. It was developed to produce the Galaksija ROM disassembly.
brief.how_it_works: The core is based largely on dz80 3.0 by Jan Panteltje, and the README says z80dasm fixes multiple bugs in it and adds features. It guesses label locations from jumps and similar instructions, unless a symbol file supplies names. The README says it handles undocumented instructions, illegal sequences and partial opcodes correctly.

brief.install_notes: No external libraries are needed. Building from a release tarball needs GNU Make and a C compiler. Building the development version from git also needs GNU Autotools. It is packaged in Debian and Ubuntu. A Windows binary exists, built by Adrien Destugues, but the README calls it outdated. Full option lists are in the z80dasm(1) man page or via --help.
brief.standout: The README stresses that z80dasm's output is reversible: a disassembly can be assembled back to the same binary, and the author says this was tested thoroughly against z80asm. It also says a lot of effort went into odd machine code such as undocumented opcodes and partial opcodes.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage gives no release date or last-commit date. The license notice covers copyright through 2026, which suggests recent work, but I could not confirm a release or commit date from the page.
brief.caveats: Developed and tested mainly on Debian GNU/Linux. The README says it should run on any sufficiently UNIX-like system, but that is untested. The Windows binary is outdated. Z180 instruction support was added only recently. Licensed under GPL v2 or later.
quotes: z80dasm is a disassembler for the Zilog Z80 microprocessor and compatibles.
Any disassembly by z80dasm is perfectly reversible with z80asm.
A lot of attention has been devoted to handling of unusual Z80 machine code.
